authentication.registrationHint: Who may create an account on this instance.

open.label: Open

invite.label: Invite only
invite.description: An account can only be created through an invite link.

closed.label: Closed
closed.description: No new accounts. Existing ones keep signing in.

authentication.signInHint: How people sign in. The options that send mail stay off until a provider is configured.
authentication.needsProvider: Set up the Email provider under Integrations first.
authentication.requireVerificationHint: A new account must confirm its address before it can sign in.
authentication.magicLinkHint: Offer signing in with a link sent by email, alongside the password.
authentication.trustProviderEmailsHint: Google and OpenID Connect sign a person in to the account that already has their address, confirmed here or not. Turn this on only where you control who can register at the provider.
authentication.emailPasswordHint: Offer the sign-in and sign-up form. Turn it off to let people in through a sign-in provider only.
authentication.needsSso: Set up a sign-in provider under Integrations first.

security.grantDescription: The 12-hour window a step-up opens for Shell, Claude Code and Codex sessions.
security.stepUpTitle: Ask for a code when opening
security.stepUpDescription: What proves it is the owner opening the terminal, every time, even on the LAN.
security.stepUpMethod: TOTP (an authenticator app), enrolled at Account -> Security. Passkey takes over once this instance runs behind HTTPS.
security.stepUpOffHint: On the LAN without a code: the terminal opens straight away for your session on the home network. Through the tunnel (loopback) and from outside, the authenticator code is always required.
security.sudoTitle: Sudo in the browser terminal asks for a password
security.sudoDescription: Off (default) leaves every sudo command passwordless everywhere, in the owner terminal exactly as much as in SSH automation -- sudo authorizes by Unix account and cannot tell the two apart. On narrows the browser terminal's sudo down to a reviewed list of automation commands and asks for the Linux password for everything else.
security.sudoHint: Turning this on here is not enough by itself: sudo cannot be switched per session at runtime, so an operator still has to audit every `sudo -n` command the instance's SSH automation runs, check it against the sudoers policy, and install that policy by hand. Ask the operator before switching this on -- until they do, this setting has no effect.
security.auditDescription: Every step-up attempt, grant change and terminal session, newest first. No keystrokes.

storage.fileSizeHint: The largest single file an upload may carry. A bigger file is refused before it is stored.
storage.attachmentHint: Applies to issue attachments, files pasted into a description, and attachments added by agents.
storage.avatarHint: The profile picture people upload for their account.
storage.mimeTypesHint: One content type per line. Leave empty to accept any file.
storage.mimeTypesNote: A line is a full type (application/pdf) or a wildcard (image/*). Files already stored are kept whatever the list says.
storage.quotaHint: Total attachment storage one project may use. 0 means no limit.
storage.quotaNote: Once a project reaches the quota, new uploads are refused until someone deletes attachments.

telegram.botConfigured: People connect their Telegram account by opening a chat with this bot from their profile.
telegram.botMissing: Create a bot with @BotFather in Telegram and paste its token here.
telegram.botTokenHint: The token is verified with Telegram when you save, so a wrong one is refused here rather than failing silently later.
telegram.resolvedHint: Resolved from the token. This is the bot people will see when connecting.

email.providerHint: Choose one provider. Credentials are stored encrypted.
email.fromHint: Required for Resend. With SMTP it defaults to the username.
email.teamNotificationsHint: Let teams deliver their notifications through this provider instead of configuring one of their own. Each team still chooses whether to use it.
email.testHint: Send a real message with the current settings without saving them.
email.testConfigureFirst: Enable a provider and add its required credentials first.

authProvider.googleMissing: Add the client ID and secret first.
authProvider.redirectUriHint: Register this on the OAuth client in the Google Cloud console. Google refuses the sign-in if it does not match exactly.
authProvider.oidcConfigured: An address without an account gets one; an address that already has a confirmed account signs into it.
authProvider.oidcMissing: Add the discovery URL, client ID and secret first.
authProvider.discoveryUrlHint: Your provider's .well-known/openid-configuration. The authorization, token and userinfo endpoints are read from it.
authProvider.oidcLabelHint: Names your provider on the sign-in button. Leave it empty for a generic label.
authProvider.scopesHint: Separated by spaces. openid is required; profile and email fill in the name and address.
authProvider.oidcRedirectUriHint: Register this as a redirect URI on the client at your identity provider. The provider refuses the sign-in if it does not match exactly.
